land.text: the kingdom after Gentius's defeat at Scodra in 168, which the Romans divided into three administrative divisions called merides (Gentius page): the Labeates and the district of Acruvium, Rhizon and Olcinium (the first division's extent is unknown)

successors.note: Ballaios, 'perhaps 167-135', ruled the Ardiaei from Rhizon after 168 (Gentius page); the Illyrian kingdom page's infobox says 'Disestablished: 135 BC' against its own text, 'after 168'.

capitals.name: Rhizon (Risan)
capitals.note: 'From the 3rd century BC to 168 BC the capital cities of the Ardiaean State were Rhizon and Scodra'; Ballaios ruled 'over Rhizon' (Illyrian kingdom page). Joint capital with Scodra.

capitals.name: Scodra (Shkodër)
capitals.note: Joint capital with Rhizon; Gentius's capital was Scodra (Gentius page), where he was defeated in 168.

rulers.name: Pleuratus II
rulers.note: The page's list gives 'c. 260-250'; the dossier starts in 256 with Cliopatria's row. Ballaios 'c. 260-c. 230' ruled over Rhizon beside him (coins only).

rulers.name: Agron
rulers.note: Infobox 250-231 BC; 'Agron died in the winter of 231 BC' (Agron page); the Illyrian kingdom page's list says 250-230.

rulers.name: Pinnes (under the regencies of Teuta and Demetrius of Pharos)
rulers.title: King, a child; regents Teuta (231-228) and then Demetrius of Pharos
rulers.note: Ardiaei page: Teuta 231-228, Demetrius 'fl. c. 228-219', Pinnes 220-after 217; the Illyrian kingdom page lists Pinnes 230-217 and Demetrius 222-219.

rulers.name: Scerdilaidas
rulers.note: Page list 218-206; 'allied with Rome to defeat Macedonia in 208 BC'.

rulers.name: Pleuratus III
rulers.note: 'rewarded by the Romans in 196 BC, with lands annexed by the Macedonians'.

rulers.name: Gentius
rulers.note: 'He ruled in 181-168 BC'; the last attested king, defeated at Scodra in 168 and taken to Rome in 167.

keyframe_review.note: 256-248, 29.6 k km2, bbox 19.0-21.2 E, Albania, North Macedonia and Kosovo: the inland Albanian core with Scodra inside but Rhizon (18.7 E) outside its western edge. The pages give no extent for these years (the Illyrian kingdom infobox says 'Area: not given'), so no area ratio; the rest of the shape is unverified: page budget.

247-240, 45.3 k km2, now north to Narona (43.5 N, 17.2 E): matches 'His state stretched from Narona in Dalmatia south to the river Aoos and Korkyra' (Agron, 250-231). The page does not date the extent; 247 is Cliopatria's year (ledger, confidence 1). No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the shape without Corcyra: the First Illyrian War page has the Illyrian fleet besiege Corcyra in the 229 season and garrison it under Demetrius of Pharos; the Agron page says only that Agron annexed the islands of Korkyra and Pharos, undated

keyframe_review.note: 239-231, 49.7 k km2, south to 39.6 N (Corfu). The Epirote coast and Epidamnus stand on the Agron page (undated); Corcyra is dated 229 by the war page, so the island is removed until the 229 gain. Disagreement between the two pages is recorded in the ledger.

correction.text: the 230 shape without Corcyra, valid for 230-229 only; Corcyra is in the kingdom for part of 229 (ledger) and from 228 the kingdom is the core north of the Drin (new keyframe illyrian-kingdom_-228)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws this 46.1 k km2 shape to 226 and then ends the row; the First Illyrian War page has the Romans land in 229 and the treaty "Before the end of winter", after which the kingdom lost, in the page's account, all its conquests south of the Drin. Phoenice, taken after the 231 campaign, was returned under a truce (undated): the cells near 40 N, 20 E that leave the shape in 230 may be that return. After the treaty Teuta kept her core territory north of the Drin (the page's account); the Greek towns Epidamnos, Apollonia and Corcyra passed under Roman protection. The extent between 228 and 197 is otherwise unverified: page budget (the Illyrian kingdom page has Scerdilaidas allied with Rome in 208 and no land change). Second Illyrian War (220-219) not opened.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 180 BC, during his early reign, the Dalmatae and Daorsi declared themselves independent.' Gentius is defeated at Scodra in 168 and the Romans divide the land into three merides.

region.text: Scodra and Rhizon, the two capitals of the Ardiaean State, and the inland shape Cliopatria draws

ledger.note: 256: the Ardiaean kingdom, the Illyrian kingdom of the Adriatic coast, stands at Scodra and Rhizon. Cliopatria's row begins here; no page opened dates a founding: the Illyrian kingdom page lists Pleuratus II 'c. 260-250' and Ballaios 'c. 260-c. 230', and the Ardiaei page has the capitals Rhizon and Scodra 'from the 3rd century BC'.

region.text: the coast and hinterland north of Scodra to Narona in Dalmatia

ledger.note: c. 247: the kingdom reaches north to Narona. 'His state stretched from Narona in Dalmatia south to the river Aoos and Korkyra' (Agron, who ruled 250-231); the page dates none of the annexations and 247 is Cliopatria's year for the shape that reaches Narona.

region.text: the coast of Epirus south of Epidamnus to the river Aoos that the 239 shape adds, without Corcyra

ledger.note: c. 239: the kingdom reaches the Epirote coast. The page has Agron annex part of Epirus and Epidamnus and garrison them (undated, within 250-231); 239 is Cliopatria's year. The same page dates the Epirote change: "In 234 BC, the royal succession in Epirus came to an end, and a federal republic was instituted."

231: Scerdilaidas takes Phoenice. 'On the way home, Teuta sent her general Scerdilaidas to capture the city of Phoenice in Epirus', after the 231 campaign against Elis and Messenia; the page dates the campaign, not the capture, and has Phoenice returned later under a truce.

c. 230: Phoenice returned. The page has Phoenice returned under a truce and the Illyrians withdraw, undated; the cells near 40 N, 20 E that Cliopatria's 230 shape no longer holds are read as this return.

229: Teuta takes Corcyra. The page has Corcyra taken and placed under a garrison led by Demetrius of Pharos after the Illyrian fleet besieged it in the 229 season. The Agron page has Agron annex Korkyra earlier, undated; Cliopatria draws it from 239.

region.text: the Adriatic ports Corcyra, Epidamnos and Apollonia and the Parthini and Atintani behind them

ledger.note: 229: Rome lands in Illyria. 'The Roman invasion of Illyria in 229 BC appears to have caught Teuta completely off guard': Fulvius's fleet reached Corcyra and Albinus crossed to Apollonia, which joined the Roman alliance.
229: Corcyra goes over to Rome. "Corcyra welcomed the Romans and, with the aid of Demetrius, surrendered its garrison"; the island would henceforward rely on Roman protection.

intersect.text: everything south of Lissus at the mouth of the Drin (Lezhe, about 41.8 N): 'all conquests south of the Drin'

region.text: the Greek towns, the Parthini and Atintani and the Epirote land south of the Drin

ledger.note: 228: the treaty strips the south. After the 229-228 war Teuta lost all her conquests south of the Drin and the ports of Epidamnos and Apollonia (the page's summary of the terms); she had to promise "not to sail south of Lissus at the mouth of the Drin with more than two ships". The treaty came "Before the end of winter", i.e. 228; the Illyrian kingdom page says 227.

intersect.text: everything south of Lissus at the mouth of the Drin (Lezhe, about 41.8 N): 'all conquests south of the Drin'

region.text: the Greek towns, the Parthini and Atintani and the Epirote land south of the Drin

ledger.note: 228: the First Illyrian War ends in a treaty; Rome "established a protectorate over these Greek towns" (Epidamnos, Apollonia, Corcyra, Pharos) and took the Parthini and Atintani as clients.

region.text: Lissus, read as the land Macedon had annexed

ledger.note: 196: Pleuratus III is 'rewarded by the Romans in 196 BC, with lands annexed by the Macedonians'. The page names no land; Lissus (Lezhe) is the researcher's bridge (Gentius's page has Lissus as the southernmost city of the kingdom; the antigonid-dynasty dossier has Philip V take Lissus in 213).

region.text: the Dalmatae and Daorsi, in central Dalmatia and the Neretva valley

ledger.note: 180: 'In 180 BC, during his early reign, the Dalmatae and Daorsi declared themselves independent.' The page does not draw their land; Dalmatia is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the kingdom's last lands, the Labeates around Scodra and the district of Acruvium, Rhizon and Olcinium

ledger.note: 168: Gentius is defeated at Scodra. "In 168 BC, he was defeated at Scodra by a Roman force under L. Anicius Gallus"; the Romans then divided the region into three merides.

168: the last Illyrian kingdom falls. Gentius, 'the last attested Illyrian king', was taken to Rome as a captive in 167; the Illyrian kingdom page has the kingdom defeated 'in 168 BC during the Third Illyrian War'. Ballaios, 'perhaps 167-135', held Rhizon afterwards.

wars.name: Medion campaign against the Aetolians
wars.outcome: Agron's Illyrians defeated the Aetolians at Medion; Agron died in the winter of 231, within a few days of the Aetolian victory (Agron page).
wars.note: 'The Illyrian attack under Agron, mounted in either 232 or 231 BC, is described by Polybius.' No land changed hands.

wars.name: First Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Rome landed in 229, took the Greek towns and the Parthini and Atintani under protection and, by the treaty of winter 229/228, cut the Illyrians off south of Lissus and the Drin; the core north of the Drin stayed with Teuta.
wars.note: The page: 'lasted from 229 BC to 228 BC'; the Illyrian kingdom page dates the submission to 227. Epidamnos was attacked but not taken on the war page, while the Agron page has Agron annex it earlier.

wars.name: Third Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Gentius, who had gone over to Perseus in 169, was defeated at Scodra by L. Anicius Gallus in 168 and the kingdom ended.
wars.note: The Gentius page does not use the name 'Third Illyrian War' (the Illyrian kingdom page does) and gives 'twenty or thirty days' for the campaign.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is Agron's 'from Narona ... south to the river Aoos and Korkyra'.
The one line the pages name is the treaty limit of 228 at Lissus and the mouth of the Drin; north of it the borders are soft.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Illyrian Kingdom' (-256..-226, 4 shapes) is the Ardiaean kingdom of Pleuratus II, Agron and Teuta; the row ends in 226 although the Illyrian kingdom page keeps the same kingdom to Gentius (168), so the dossier runs to 168 and carries three new keyframes (228, 196, 180) at low precision. Start 256 is Cliopatria's year: no page dates a founding (the list has Pleuratus II and Ballaios from c. 260; the infobox 'Established: c. 500 BC' and Bardylis c. 400 belong to earlier Illyrian dynasties of other tribes (Dardani, Taulantii) and are not drawn here). Disagreements between pages: Corcyra annexed by Agron (undated, Agron page) or taken in 229 (First Illyrian War page; followed); Epidamnos annexed by Agron or only attacked in 229; peace in winter 229/228 (war page) or 227 (Illyrian kingdom page); Agron's death 231 (text) or 230 (list); Demetrius of Pharos 228-219 (Ardiaei) or 222-219 (list); kingdom ended 168 (text) or 135 (infobox). Not on any page opened and left out: Pharos and Issa (islands off Dalmatia), the Second Illyrian War of 220-219 and Demetrius's fall (218), the Atintani/Parthini borders, the extent in 227-197 (the 228 keyframe is the treaty reading), the land rewarded in 196. Counterparts without a dossier: Corcyra (Corfu), Epidamnos, Apollonia, the Dalmatae and Daorsi, the Parthini and Atintani; kingdom-of-epirus has no matching loss for 239 and 231. Gazetteer names needed: Phoenice (Finiq), Rhizon (Risan) as places; the polygon cut at 41.78 N stands in for 'south of the Drin'.
